result.summary: The street environment lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure at the intersection, including marked crosswalks and curb ramps. While a sidewalk exists on the left, the right side is heavily overgrown with vegetation, and the wide, unmarked roadway may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, increasing exposure and making pedestrian movements less predictable for drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: No curb ramps are visible at the corner, creating a barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.

hazards.name: Overgrown Vegetation
hazards.description: Dense vegetation on the right side of the street obstructs the pedestrian path and limits visibility.

interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at the intersection corners to ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of infrastructure on one side and a poorly maintained, narrow sidewalk on the other. The absence of marked crossings, combined with significant pavement degradation and sightline obstructions from parked cars and vegetation, creates a high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or on uneven dirt.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The road surface is heavily cracked and patched, creating tripping hazards and uneven surfaces for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the roadway

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Overgrown vegetation and parked vehicles on the left side block visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, separated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway and repair the existing sidewalk to eliminate tripping hazards and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Remove overgrown vegetation and restrict parking near potential crossing points to improve visibility between all road users.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide but poorly maintained sidewalk running alongside a large brick institutional building. The environment lacks any physical separation between pedestrians and the roadway, and the pavement surfaces are significantly degraded with cracks and patches.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: The sidewalk exhibits significant cracking, uneven patching, and surface deterioration, creating trip hazards.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian-Vehicle Separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer, such as trees, bollards, or a furniture zone, between the walking area and the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the sidewalk adjacent to the street
